verses.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh. I have made him and his officials stubborn so that I can do these signs of mine among them.
And I did this so that you can tell your children and grandchildren how hard I was on the Egyptians, and about the signs I did among them. Then you will know that I am the LORD."

So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: 'How long will you refuse to humble yourself in front of me? Let my people go, so that they can worship me.
If you refuse to let them go, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your country.
They will cover the ground so that it cannot be seen. They will eat whatever little you have left after the hail, including every tree that is growing in your fields.

They will fill your houses, and the houses of all your officials and all the Egyptians. Neither your parents nor your grandparents have ever seen anything like it, from the day they settled in this land until now.'" Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh.
Pharaoh's officials said to him, "How long will this man be a trap for us? Let the people go, so that they can worship the LORD their God. Do you not see yet that Egypt is ruined?"
So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. He said to them, "Go, worship the LORD your God. But tell me who will be going."
Moses answered, "We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and our daughters, and with our flocks and herds, because we are to hold a feast for the LORD."
Pharaoh said, "The LORD would really have to be with you if I let you go with your children! Clearly you are planning something evil.
No! Only the men may go and worship the LORD, since that is what you have been asking for." Then Moses and Aaron were driven out of Pharaoh's presence.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over Egypt so that locusts will swarm over the land and eat every plant, everything the hail has left."
So Moses stretched out his staff over Egypt, and the LORD made an east wind blow across the land all that day and all that night. By morning the wind had brought the locusts.
The locusts came over the whole land of Egypt and settled down everywhere. There had never been so many locusts before, and there never will be again.

They covered the whole ground until it was black. They ate everything growing in the fields and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left. Nothing green was left on any tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh quickly called for Moses and Aaron and said, "I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
Now please forgive my sin just this once more, and pray to the LORD your God to take this deadly plague away from me."
Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD.
Then the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind. It picked up the locusts and blew them into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt.
But the LORD made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he would not let the people of Israel go.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky, so that darkness will cover Egypt, darkness so thick that people can feel it."
So Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and total darkness covered all of Egypt for three days.
No one could see anyone else, and no one left his place for three days. But all the people of Israel had light where they lived.
Then Pharaoh called for Moses and said, "Go and worship the LORD. Even your children may go with you. Only leave your flocks and herds behind."
But Moses said, "You must also let us have animals for sacrifices and burnt offerings to offer to the LORD our God.

Our animals must go with us too. Not one hoof is to be left behind. We have to use some of them to worship the LORD our God, and until we get there, we will not know which ones we need to worship the LORD."
But the LORD made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he would not let them go.
Pharaoh said to Moses, "Get out of my sight! Make sure you never see my face again! The day you see my face, you will die."
Moses replied, "Just as you say. I will never see your face again."
